title: Unit 3: Exercise 2 - Making Allowances for Your Kids' Dollar Values

parts.title: Part 1
parts.content:
1 Would you stoop to pick up a found penny? If you believe in the value of money or the possibility of luck, you would. Unless, of course, you're a teenager. When Nuveen Investments asked 1,000 kids aged 12 to 17 to name the sum they would bother to pick up, 58 per cent said a dollar or more. Some won't give pocket space to coins even if they're already in hand, says Neale Godfrey, author of Money Doesn't Grow on Trees. Many high schoolers buy lunch and throw away the change, she says. As one boy explained to her, "What am I going to do with it?"


2 This cavalier attitude is making some parents rethink the allowance tradition. The weekly stipend is meant to help kids learn about money, but some experts say too much cash — easily handed out in these flush times — and too few obligations can lead to a fiscally irresponsible future. Many kids have a "lack of understanding (of) how hard it is to earn money," says Godfrey. "That is not OK."


3 Allowances, done right, are a way to teach children to plan ahead and choose wisely, to balance saving, spending, investing, and even philanthropy. Doing it right means deciding ahead of time how much to give and how often to give it. And it requires determining what the child's responsibilities will be.


4 About 50 per cent of children between 12 and 18 get an allowance or cash from their parents, says a survey conducted in 1997 by Ohio State University for the US Labor Department. The median amount they got was $50 a week. (Teenagers in the East North Central region, which includes Ohio and Indiana, get the most — a median of $75 a week — and kids in the East South Central, including Mississippi and Alabama, are given the least, with a median of $30 a week.) Nationally speaking, about 10 million kids receive a total of around $1 billion every week.


5 The problem with a parental open-wallet policy, says Godfrey: "If you're always given money, why would it have any value to you?" Earned money is spent more wisely, she says. "You're teaching them that there is not an entitlement programme in life. The way you get it is you earn it."


6 Godfrey thinks an allowance should be chore-based, and she divides work into two categories: citizen-of-the-household chores and work-for-pay chores. "The punishment for not doing your work-for-pay chores is you don't get paid." Other experts, including Jayne Pearl, author of Kids and Money, believe that every family member is entitled to a small piece of the financial pie and that it shouldn't be tied to work. Doing so "complicates things unnecessarily and imbues allowance with power struggles and control issues," says Pearl. "I think of (an allowance) as learning capital ... . They have to have some money to practise with."


7 For many kids, 3 is a good time to begin getting an allowance, experts say. This sounds early, but it's then that children start understanding the notion of exchanging coins for, say, candy. Deciding how much to give can be tough. "If the parents can afford it, I have them pay their age per week," says Godfrey. "A 3-year-old gets $3."


8 Sound like a lot for a little person? Godfrey's plan takes 10 per cent off the top for charity. The remainder is divided into thirds and put into jars. The quick-cash jar "is for instant gratification." This spend-as-they-choose money means that candy bars, Pokémon cards, and other impulse buys are no longer paid for by Mom and Dad, which causes kids to curb many impulses. Says Godfrey of her 17-year-old daughter, Kyle: "Her Starbucks bill is her own."


9 The second jar is for medium-term savings, meant to be spent on medium-ticket luxuries like in-line skates or a CD player. The final jar is invested for the long term, such as for college.


10 Kelly Grant, 13, thinks that is fair. An eighth grader in Greenville, S.C., Kelly and his brother, Christopher, 15, each gets $15 a week. The trade-off: "I have to walk and feed the dog, and I have to do the recyclables," Kelly says. He spends but still saved enough to buy a Sony PlayStation.


11 Christopher, who has a girlfriend, spends most of what he gets; he supplements his pocket money by doing extra work, like mowing the lawn. "I'm supposed to do a load of laundry every night." He has, he admits, a tendency to forget. "They charge my allowance sometimes," he says, "but they don't really remember to do it."


12 The Grant boys are still learning about earning and show signs of valuing money. They wouldn't stop to pick up a dime, but both say there are coins they would rescue from the sidewalk. Says Christopher: "You can do a lot with a quarter."

options: A. many kids don't bother to pick up small coins.
B. few kids want one-dollar coins.
C. some kids save coins.
D. no kids want to pick up coins.
questions.answer: A. many kids don't bother to pick up small coins.
questions.explanation: Trong đoạn 1, kết quả khảo sát của Nuveen Investments cho thấy: "When Nuveen Investments asked 1,000 kids aged 12 to 17 to name the sum they would bother to pick up, 58 per cent said a dollar or more." Điều này có nghĩa là có rất nhiều trẻ không buồn nhặt những đồng tiền lẻ có mệnh giá nhỏ hơn 1 đô la. Vì vậy đáp án A là chính xác.

options: A. many kids appreciated the value of coins.
B. many kids know how hard it is to earn money.
C. many kids don't know the value of money.
D. many kids should be given more pocket money.
questions.answer: C. many kids don't know the value of money.
questions.explanation: Trong đoạn 2, Godfrey nhận định rằng: "Many kids have a 'lack of understanding (of) how hard it is to earn money'". Nhận định này đồng nghĩa với việc nhiều trẻ em không biết giá trị của đồng tiền và sự khó khăn để kiếm được chúng. Do đó đáp án C là chính xác.

options: A. should not be given to children.
B. should not be given to young children.
C. could help children learn many things.
D. spoil older children.
questions.answer: C. could help children learn many things.
questions.explanation: Trong đoạn 3, tác giả viết: "Allowances, done right, are a way to teach children to plan ahead and choose wisely, to balance saving, spending, investing, and even philanthropy." Tức là nếu được cấp tiền tiêu vặt đúng cách, trẻ có thể học được nhiều điều như lập kế hoạch, lựa chọn khôn ngoan, cân bằng tiết kiệm, chi tiêu, đầu tư và thậm chí là làm từ thiện. Do đó, đáp án C đúng.

questions.content: On average, children who receive the most allowances live in
options: A. the East North Central region.
B. the East South Central region.
C. big cities like New York or L.A..
D. small towns in New England.
questions.answer: A. the East North Central region.
questions.explanation: Trong đoạn 4 có nêu rõ: "Teenagers in the East North Central region, which includes Ohio and Indiana, get the most — a median of $75 a week". Điều này khẳng định thanh thiếu niên ở khu vực East North Central nhận được nhiều tiền tiêu vặt nhất. Vì vậy, đáp án A là chính xác.

questions.content: Which of the following would Godfrey probably agree?
options: A. Children should not be given allowances.
B. Children should receive allowances if they help with housework.
C. Children should be given allowances whether they help with housework.
D. Children should be paid for satisfactorily performing school work.
questions.answer: B. Children should receive allowances if they help with housework.
questions.explanation: Trong đoạn 6, Godfrey cho rằng: "Godfrey thinks an allowance should be chore-based". Bà phân loại công việc thành hai loại: việc nhà của thành viên trong gia đình và công việc được trả công. Do đó, Godfrey đồng tình với việc trẻ em nên được nhận tiền tiêu vặt nếu chúng phụ giúp làm việc nhà (chores). Vậy đáp án B là chính xác.

questions.content: Which of the following would Pearl probably agree?
options: A. Children should not be given allowances.
B. Children should receive allowances if they help with housework.
C. Children should be given allowances whether they help with housework.
D. Children should be paid for satisfactorily performing school work.
questions.answer: C. Children should be given allowances whether they help with housework.
questions.explanation: Khác với Godfrey, trong đoạn 6, Jayne Pearl tin rằng: "every family member is entitled to a small piece of the financial pie and that it shouldn't be tied to work." Tức là mỗi thành viên trong gia đình đều có quyền có một phần tài chính nhỏ và điều đó không nên bị ràng buộc bởi việc làm việc nhà. Do đó, đáp án C là đúng nhất.

questions.content: Who supports the idea of starting to give allowances to kids when they are three?
options: A. The writer.
B. Pearl.
C. Godfrey's daughter.
D. Godfrey.
questions.explanation: Trong đoạn 7, khi bàn về việc cho trẻ em tiền tiêu vặt từ lúc 3 tuổi, bài đọc trích dẫn ý kiến của Godfrey: "'If the parents can afford it, I have them pay their age per week,' says Godfrey. 'A 3-year-old gets $3.'" Do đó, Godfrey chính là người ủng hộ ý tưởng này. Vậy đáp án D là đúng.

questions.content: According to Godfrey, if a child has a monthly allowances of $100, how much should he/she spend on "impulse buys"?
questions.explanation: Dựa theo kế hoạch của Godfrey ở đoạn 8: Trước tiên trích 10% cho từ thiện (tức là $10 từ $100). Số tiền còn lại là $90. Sau đó chia đều làm 3 phần (vào 3 lọ), mỗi lọ là $30. Lọ tiền mặt nhanh (quick-cash jar) được dùng cho mục đích thoả mãn tức thời ("instant gratification") hay những món đồ mua theo cảm hứng ("impulse buys"). Do vậy số tiền dùng cho "impulse buys" là $30. Đáp án B là chính xác.

options: A. without having to work.
B. by doing housework.
C. but the money is not enough.
D. though their parents sometimes forget to give them the money.
questions.explanation: Trong đoạn 10, Kelly Grant (một trong hai anh em nhà Grant) chia sẻ: "The trade-off: 'I have to walk and feed the dog, and I have to do the recyclables,' Kelly says." Nghĩa là các cậu bé phải làm việc nhà (như dắt chó đi dạo, cho chó ăn, đi đổ rác tái chế...) để đổi lấy tiền tiêu vặt. Do đó đáp án B là chính xác.
